title: openai-compat: tool calling schema mapping, tool_choice semantics, and tool message formatting
author: Connor Blake
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compat layer to parity for function/tool calling semantics. This PR implements 3 coordinated pieces: (1) tool schema mapping so Redwood tools (internal typed tool defs) can be surfaced as OpenAI-style JSON Schema parameters and mapped back on invocation; (2) the tool_choice model output semantics so the compatibility layer correctly interprets both `tool` return formats and the newer `tool_choice` structured decision; and (3) normalization/formatting for tool messages (system/tool/user) so downstream SDKs receive consistent message shapes across streaming and non-streaming responses.

Summary of changes: 
- Add a bidirectional schema mapper that translates Redwood tool parameter definitions to OpenAI JSON Schema and converts validated JSON params back into typed Redwood arguments. Mapping includes support for primitives, enums, nested objects (shallow only), arrays, required/optional fields, and example/default propagation.
- Implement `tool_choice` semantics in the OpenAI-compat router: when the model returns a tool selection, we now handle both (a) `tool` call style (legacy) and (b) `tool_choice` style (structured choice with `name` + `arguments`). The router prefers explicit `tool_choice` when present, falls back to `tool` with best-effort parsing, and emits a compatibility warning in logs when fallback occurs.
- Normalize tool message formatting across streaming and non-streaming responses. Streaming messages are now emitted as partial JSON-safe fragments with an explicit `message_type` metadata token to let clients rehydrate the message on the JS/Python SDKs. Non-streaming responses produce the same final message object shape.
- SDK changes (TS + Python): helpers to register OpenAI-compatible tool schemas and utilities to parse `tool_choice` outputs into SDK-native call objects.
- Docs and migration guide: docs/openai-compat.md updated with examples and migration steps for customers relying on legacy `tool` formats.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add schema mapper implementation and unit tests
- [x] Implement `tool_choice` routing and integration tests
- [x] Add streaming normalization and SDK helpers
- [x] Update docs and add migration notes
- [x] E2E test against sample model responses

Backward compatibility: This PR aims to be backward-compatible by default. If a model returns the legacy `tool` invocation format, we attempt to parse it and convert to a `tool_choice`-like internal representation. Customers who depend on the exact raw tool payload may need to opt-in to the new behavior; see migration_notes.

Testing: Added unit tests for schema mappings, property rounding (enum/default handling), and validation errors. Integration tests simulate model outputs for both `tool` and `tool_choice` variants and assert correct router behavior. E2E uses the compat harness to validate streaming reassembly.

Related: ENG-3421 (schema mapper), ENG-3487 (tool_choice semantics), SUP-512 (customer case where a streaming tool call broke on legacy clients).

review_comments: Aisha Patel (request changes): Please add a note in schema_mapper.py about how we handle unknown enum values — should we coerce or reject?
Connor Blake (author): We now reject unknown enums and return a clear schema validation error; added tests and a migration note.
Miguel Santos: Can we avoid the compatibility warning log spam for high-throughput customers? Suggest adding a rate-limited logger or sampling.
Connor Blake: switched to sampled warnings (1/1000) and added a per-customer opt-out flag (openai_compat.warn_on_fallback=false).
Linnea Olsson (approve): Tests look good; SDK helpers are well documented. Left a minor doc nit about an example payload.
migration_notes: Defaults and enums: the schema mapper will reject unknown enum values by default. Customers who previously relied on permissive parsing should add a compatibility shim in their tool registration or set openai_compat.permissive_enum_parsing=true. For streaming clients: partial message fragments now include a `message_type` token; SDKs >= v0.14.0 rehydrate automatically. See docs/openai-compat.md for examples.
release_notes: OpenAI-compat: Add schema mapping for tool parameters, support for `tool_choice` outputs, and unified streaming/non-streaming tool message shapes. Backward-compatible with best-effort parsing of legacy `tool` formats. SDK updates required for automatic rehydration in streaming clients.
